clue.text: By killing, reduce the number of pests around in fruit

indicators.note: in means the reversed pests are placed inside the fruit

parts.note: a date is a fruit of the palm

indicators.note: around here means the pests are turned round, read from the end

parts.note: mice are household pests

explanation.surface: A gardener thins out the vermin infesting his fruit crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the pests to ECIM before they go 'in' the fruit; 'fruit' at the end looks like part of the pest story but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally meaning to kill one in ten, the verb now means to destroy a large share of something.

clue.text: Dreadful textile worker, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a dyer colours cloth

explanation.surface: A cloth worker is said to be terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire is a synonym of dreadful, meaning extremely bad.

clue.text: . About time to lock up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, Latin for about
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: It's about time someone was locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage is to confine or imprison, a synonym of lock up.

clue.text: Slips in road races

parts.note: the M1 motorway is written MI in crosswords
sprints are short fast races

explanation.surface: Runners take tumbles during road races.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first motorway, from London to Yorkshire; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a slip in printing, a typographical error.

clue.text: In bezique, one must be especially helpful

definitions.text: In bezique, one must be especially helpful

parts.words: In bezique, one must be especially helpful
parts.note: read literally, a player in the card game bezique must reveal winning cards; read as idiom, it means come through for someone unexpectedly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to prove unexpectedly useful, from revealing a winning suit in a card game.

clue.text: Excellent policeman beginning on beat

parts.note: a super is a superintendent, a senior police officer

indicators.note: beginning on asks for the first letter of the word beat

explanation.surface: A fine officer starts out walking his beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is a synonym of excellent, meaning of the very highest quality.

clue.text: Custom America, say, rejected

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: An American custom is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means customary practice, a synonym of custom.

clue.text: Comfortably settling: NCO's who've been trained in unfeminine method of fighting

indicators.note: in means the drilled officers go inside the other piece
unfeminine means the abbreviation F for feminine is removed

parts.note: fencing is fighting with swords

indicators.note: trained means put through drill, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Non-commissioned officers settle in after learning a manly combat style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfeminine' takes F from FENCING, leaving ENCING; NCOS rearranged ('who've been trained') to SCON goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensconce is to settle oneself snugly, so ensconcing is comfortably settling.

clue.text: Popular book, first Peter never finished

parts.note: best means first or top

indicators.note: never finished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Peter Sellers was a British comic actor

explanation.surface: Peter never got to the end of the top-selling book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never finished' takes the final S from SELLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestseller is a book that sells in great numbers, so a popular one.

clue.text: Place to keep records concerning point and line

parts.note: re means concerning or about
the gist is the main point of something
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An archive holding documents on a point and a line, like a geometry office.
explanation.definitionFit: A registry is an office or place where official records are stored.

clue.text: A large proportion of USA snakes .. seen about in region round Topeka

indicators.note: seen about means the run is read turned round, from right to left
a large proportion of says most of the letters of the words that follow are taken, not all

explanation.surface: Most American snakes are found around the area of a Midwestern city.
explanation.walkthrough: From USA SNAKES take most, USASNAK, and 'seen about' turns it to read KANSASU; the run KANSAS sits within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the state capital of Kansas, so the region round it is that state.

clue.text: Criticism still surrounds Scottish town in a predicament

parts.note: stick means harsh criticism, as in getting stick

indicators.note: surrounds means the word for still goes round the town

parts.note: yet means still
Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: Censure continues to hang over a Highland town in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounds' puts the town inside the word for still. The phrase comes from cricket, where a damp pitch makes batting hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky wicket is an idiom for an awkward, difficult situation.

clue.text: Dispute decision involving tough teasers

indicators.note: involving in its sense of entangling or complicating tells us the letters of tough teasers are mixed up

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a ruling about hard puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like a link but is the anagram signal; the twelve letters of TOUGH TEASERS rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to dispute a decision already made, from contesting a coin toss.

clue.text: I rearranged cake tins grand sport

indicators.note: rearranged means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone tidies baking tins, a grand pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: I and CAKE TINS 'rearranged' give ICESKATIN; G follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-skating is a sport and pastime of gliding on ice.

clue.text: Luncheon voucher sought by gold-digger?

definitions.meaning: literally, a ticket exchanged for a meal
figuratively, a person seen as a source of income, which a fortune hunter seeks

explanation.definitionFit: A literal ticket for food, or figuratively someone exploited as a source of money.

clue.text: Not prohibited completely

definitions.meaning: ... describes something free of banned substances or permitted, as a ... athlete
... as an adverb means entirely, as in ... forgot

explanation.definitionFit: Clean means free of banned things, and as an adverb it means wholly, as in clean through.

clue.text: Start to call chatline, bothered by this sort of fault?

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed or upset, so these letters are thrown into a new order
start to means the first letter of the word call

explanation.surface: Ringing a chat service, someone is irritated by a recurring glitch on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' mixes C (from 'Start to call') with CHATLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical fault is a mechanical or equipment failure, the kind a phone line might suffer.

clue.text: Go variant played by Henry?

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are moved about like pieces in a game

explanation.surface: A form of the board game Go is played by someone named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Henry the Navigator was a 15th-century Portuguese patron of exploration.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry the Navigator is the epithet of the Portuguese prince, so the clue's Henry evokes the title.

clue.text: Former name of capital prime minister

definitions.meaning: Harare, capital of Zimbabwe, was called ... under colonial rule
the Marquess of ... was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.definitionFit: Harare in Zimbabwe once bore this name, which also belonged to a three-time Victorian premier.

clue.text: Something is happening here planet finally changes direction

indicators.note: finally changes direction says the last letter, a compass point, is swapped for another point

parts.note: Venus is a planet

explanation.surface: Big news: a planet has at last altered its course.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of VENUS is S, south; changing it to E, east, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where an event is held, so where something happens.

clue.text: Miss Liddell's name is suppressed. by prudes in this town

parts.note: Alice Liddell was the girl for whom Lewis Carroll wrote Alice in Wonderland

indicators.note: suppressed by means held in by, so the name abbreviation goes inside the prudes

parts.note: prigs are self-righteous prudes

explanation.surface: Prudish townsfolk hush up the name of Lewis Carroll's young muse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressed by' puts N inside the prudes, giving PRINGS. Alice Springs is a town in central Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's this town points at a real place, a town in Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Computer that's providing support for English servicemen

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that props up the others sits below them

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, gives servicemen
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A machine props up some English soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks winning UK Premium Bond numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: This British random-number machine is a famous computer, the Premium Bond draw generator.

clue.text: Fell from bird-watchers' retreat

definitions.meaning: a fell is an animal's skin or pelt
a shelter where bird-watchers wait out of sight

explanation.definitionFit: An animal's pelt, or a concealed shelter for observing wildlife.

clue.text: Almost excel in climb

indicators.note: almost means the word is taken short of its final letter

parts.note: to shine is to excel

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stands out on an ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: To shin up is to climb using arms and legs, so shin means climb.

clue.text: Blackening popular monarch

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A well-loved king has his name blackened.
explanation.definitionFit: Inking means covering with ink, making something black.

clue.text: Keep quiet about equipment — it's unpredictable

indicators.note: about means the call for silence goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
kit means equipment
'tis is an old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: Say nothing about the gear: it behaves erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: SH goes 'about' KIT and TIS ('tis, an old form of it's).
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish describes a nervous, capricious horse or person, hard to predict.

clue.text: Collect the fish outside

indicators.note: outside means the fish surrounds the word the

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Fetch the fish waiting out there.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is a synonym of collect, bringing things together.

clue.text: Vet admits little time for fish

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the short time goes inside

parts.note: a vet is a veterinary surgeon
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An animal doctor briefly takes in a fish for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like a verb but stands for the noun, short for veterinary surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, the source of caviar.
